gloss: to show off; to try to look cool

definitions.gloss: to show off; to try to look cool; to put on airs
definitions.explanation: To deliberately behave or dress in a way intended to impress others, often with the implication of being somewhat vain or pretentious.

examples.japanese: そんなに{格好|かっこう}つけなくていいよ。
examples.english: You don't have to show off like that.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{女|おんな}の{子|こ}の{前|まえ}だと{格好|かっこう}つけたがる。
examples.english: He likes to show off in front of girls.

examples.japanese: {格好|かっこう}つけないで、{素直|すなお}に{助|たす}けてって{言|い}えばいいのに。
examples.english: Instead of trying to look cool, you should just be honest and ask for help.

notes:
A colloquial expression used when someone is consciously trying to appear impressive, stylish, or tough. Often carries a mildly critical or teasing nuance, implying the person is being somewhat fake or pretentious. Very common in casual conversation, especially among younger speakers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {格好|かっこう}つけたがる: to like showing off
- {格好|かっこう}つけないで: stop trying to look cool
- {格好|かっこう}つけて{話|はな}す: to speak in a showy way
- いつも{格好|かっこう}つけている: always trying to look cool

USAGE:
The shortened form かっこつける is also very common in casual speech. Conjugates as an ichidan verb: {格好|かっこう}つけない (negative), {格好|かっこう}つけて (te-form), etc.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {気取|きど}る: to put on airs, to act affected (slightly more literary; focuses on pretending to be refined)
- {見栄|みえ}を{張|は}る: to keep up appearances, to put on a show (emphasizes doing things beyond one's means to impress)
- {背伸|せの}びする: to stretch beyond one's abilities, to try to appear more capable than one is
